note: Synthesised candidates, not anonymised ones. Every name, employer, institution and date is invented; what is drawn from reality is the SHAPE — a career changer whose strongest evidence is a long-running side project, a contractor with overlapping engagements, a front-end engineer whose real skills live in prose rather than in the skills list, a graduate with a skills section longer than their CV. Anonymising real profiles would leave re-identifiable combinations of employer, dates and title; synthesising from patterns does not, and costs nothing here because the benchmark measures judgment, not provenance.

profiles.label: Mid-level backend engineer, well-documented
profiles.summary: Seven years of Python work with clean structured data: skills are listed, roles are dated, and descriptions corroborate the skills. The easy case, included so the benchmark has a baseline where a matcher should not struggle.

experiences.description: Built and maintained Django REST services for freight tracking. Designed PostgreSQL schemas and Celery task pipelines. Deployed on AWS ECS behind a Docker build.
Python services for ad delivery. Introduced Docker-based local development and continuous integration.

projects.name: Routewise
projects.description: Weekend project for cycling route planning.

profiles.label: Mechanical engineer moving into software
profiles.summary: Six years of mechanical engineering, then two and a half years of paid web development — but a self-maintained Django project running since 2020. The case that separates 'has done this for years' from 'has been paid to do this for years', and the one where a bachelor's in the wrong subject meets 'or related field'.

experiences.description: Mechanical design for industrial pump assemblies. Automated CAD reporting with Python scripts.
Small business websites and internal tools built with Django and PostgreSQL.

projects.name: OpenLedger
projects.description: Open-source bookkeeping tool, maintained single-handedly since 2020. Around 900 GitHub stars.

profiles.label: Infrastructure contractor with overlapping engagements
profiles.summary: Three engagements, two of which overlap by nearly three years. Summing them gives ten years of experience; merging them gives eight and a half. Also carries one live certification and one that lapsed, and a regulated-banking engagement that a domain requirement should be able to see.

experiences.description: Kubernetes platform for a regulated retail bank. Terraform-managed AWS accounts inside PCI-DSS scope, working to BaFin audit requirements.
Go services and Helm charts for an e-commerce platform. Ran concurrently with the Meridian engagement.
Go and Kubernetes for a clinical scheduling platform handling patient data.

profiles.label: Front-end engineer whose real skills are only in prose
profiles.summary: Six years of front-end work. The skills list names only the basics; React, TypeScript, Jest and Playwright appear solely inside role descriptions — which is how a great many real profiles are written. Also contains the counter-example: a technology mentioned as evaluated and abandoned, which is a mention that should NOT become experience.

experiences.description: Built and shipped the customer dashboard in React with TypeScript. Owned the component library and migrated it to styled-components. Wrote the Jest unit suite and the Playwright end-to-end tests.
jQuery and vanilla JavaScript for a tour booking site. Evaluated React Native for a companion mobile app, but the project was cancelled before any code shipped.

profiles.label: Senior ML engineer, eleven years, doctorate
profiles.summary: The seniority and domain case. Led a team, owned model governance at a regulated lender, holds a PhD in a quantitative subject that is not named 'Computer Science'. Everything a posting asks for at this level is present in the document and almost none of it is in a structured field.

experiences.description: Lead four engineers building credit-risk models for a regulated consumer lender. PyTorch and Spark on a shared feature store. Own model governance and the FCA model-risk documentation.
Demand forecasting models for logistics clients, in Python and scikit-learn.

profiles.label: Recent graduate with a skills list longer than the CV
profiles.summary: One six-month internship, one capstone project, and a skills section naming seven technologies — four of which nothing else in the profile touches. Extremely common, and the case that asks whether a matcher can tell a corroborated claim from an unsupported one.

experiences.description: Six-month internship. Wrote Python scripts for internal reporting and fixed bugs in a React admin page.

projects.name: Timetabler
projects.description: Final-year capstone: a Flask web application for university timetabling.

profiles.label: Engineer working in Hamburg
profiles.summary: A single ongoing role in a German city that is not the one a Berlin posting names. Included to separate 'same city' from 'same country', which are different questions a reader answers differently.
